repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until(not ((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true))
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate polls the motion sensor only at the start of the 1-second cycle. The IR requires a rising-edge wait, meaning it must block until the transition from false to true occurs. Evidence F2 shows the input went true at t=100ms, but the candidate emitted no action because its `if` guard evaluated to false at t=0 and never waited for the edge.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` with a rising-edge state machine using `wait until`. This ensures the script blocks until the motion sensor transitions to true, then executes the body, matching the IR's `wait(cond, edge rising)` semantics.
